title: Pork and Apple Casserole
subtitle: Braised pork shoulder with cider, apples, and mustard
excerpt: Pork shoulder slowly braised in cider with sweet apples, thyme, and a generous spoonful of wholegrain mustard. A simple autumn casserole that needs almost no attention.

recipe.sourceNotes: Pork and apple is one of the most natural flavour pairings in British cooking. Pigs were traditionally kept in orchards, feeding on windfalls, and the affinity between the meat and the fruit is deep-rooted in rural British and Norman cooking. Cider, made from the same apples, reinforces the connection. The West Country tradition of cooking pork in cider (porc normande in French cooking) uses cider as both a braising liquid and a flavouring, with the alcohol cooking off to leave a gentle fruitiness. Adding apple pieces to the casserole itself creates a sweet, melting contrast to the rich, fatty pork. Wholegrain mustard stirred in at the end gives a sharpness that cuts through the richness of the dish.

recipeTools.notes: A large casserole dish or deep roasting tin with a lid.

content.text: Pork shoulder has enough fat to braise for 2 hours without drying out. Do not use lean pork loin for this dish: it will become tough and dry under extended cooking. Add the apple pieces in the last 30 minutes of cooking so they soften without completely dissolving. Stir in the mustard and cream (if using) off the heat or over low heat only, to prevent splitting.

items.preparation: Cox or Braeburn, peeled, cored, and quartered

content.text: Toss the pork with the flour, salt, and pepper. Heat the oil in a large casserole over high heat. Brown the pork in batches until golden on all sides. Remove and set aside.
Reduce to medium. Fry the onion for 5 minutes until softened. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Return the pork. Pour in the cider and stock. Add the thyme and bay. Bring to a simmer.

Cook covered over a very low simmer (or in the oven at 160 C / fan 140 C) for 1 hour 30 minutes. Add the apple pieces and cook for a further 30 minutes until the pork is completely tender. Remove the thyme and bay. Stir in the wholegrain mustard. Taste for seasoning. Serve with mashed potato.
